headline: Wildfire health study finds uneven recovery for Maui survivors

meeting.body: Maui County Council Water Authority, Social Services, and Parks Committee
meeting.summary: Researchers told the committee wildfire recovery is uneven, with jobs up but severe food insecurity and children's mental health concerns remaining.
meeting.recap: The committee received an update on the Maui Wildfire Exposure Cohort Study, a health study of wildfire survivors.[[0:11:47]] Researchers said recovery is underway but uneven.[[0:13:39]] Temporary housing among adults in the study fell from about 4 in 10 to about 3 in 10.[[0:16:48]] The study has completed more than 4,000 appointments involving over 2,500 children and adults since January 2024.[[0:21:26]] Among adults who came back for follow-up, employment rose from 62% to nearly 81%.[[0:23:06]] About 23% of participants remain severely food insecure, which researchers said is unchanged.[[0:25:03]] Researchers hope to serve 1,000 more residents, mainly children, through a program called Hoʻala starting in January.[[0:29:49]] Among children, low self-esteem rose from about 13% to 26%.[[0:30:54]] Researchers asked council members to help find schools, churches, community centers and housing sites for free screenings.[[0:31:55]] A wildfire survivor testified and asked that subcontractors and nonprofit spending be audited.[[0:41:08]] A researcher said the share of participants with poor lung function rose about 5%, for reasons not yet known.[[0:47:26]]
decided: Administration staff were named resource personnel (experts who can answer questions) without objection.
Members agreed without objection to hear the presentation before public testimony.
Oral testimony was closed without objection.
meeting.next: Researchers said they will share an upcoming paper on lung function differences across Maui with the committee once it is released. A researcher said they may contact council members to identify spaces in each district for screenings and support. The committee planned a second round of questions after the break.

moments.q: "Recovery is underway, but it remains uneven."
"I don't even think Lahaina is in recovery yet."

issues.oneLine: Temporary housing among adults in the wildfire study fell from about 4 in 10 to about 3 in 10.
issues.why: The study said housing uncertainty can make it harder to sleep, manage stress, get to appointments and keep children in school.
issues.brief: The study said many survivors are still living in temporary housing.[[#1]] A clinician said patients worry about FEMA making them leave at the end of the month.[[#2]]

issues.oneLine: A wildfire health study found food insecurity improved slightly but remains high.
issues.why: The study said food insecurity affects stress, blood pressure, mental health and family well-being.

deadlines.t: Second reading of the food security and nutrition plan.

issues.brief: Food hardship among participants improved from about 49.8% to 44.9%.[[#1]] About 23% of participants, or one in four, remain severely food insecure.[[#2]] The study said many families are still stretching meals and worrying about groceries.[[#3]]
